classification.difficultyReason: Uses the supplied intersections to sketch both curves, determines that their vertical order reverses at x=2, and constructs two oppositely ordered difference integrals so the enclosed areas add rather than cancel.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the curves $y=\dfrac{6}{x}$ and $y=x^2-6x+11$ intersect when $x=1$, $2$ and $3$.

answer.short: The points $(1,6)$, $(2,3)$ and $(3,2)$ lie on both curves.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Graph these two curves and shade the two areas enclosed by them.

answer.short: Shade the regions between the curves for $1\le x\le2$ and $2\le x\le3$.
answer.worked: The curves intersect at $(1,6)$, $(2,3)$ and $(3,2)$. The parabola is above the hyperbola on $1<x<2$, and the hyperbola is above the parabola on $2<x<3$. Shade these two enclosed regions.

spec.description: Focused positive-domain view showing all three intersections; exact two enclosed regions have stronger blue fill and labelled leader arrows R1/R2, with no enlargement of their geometry.
spec.mathematics: y=6/x and y=(x-3)^2+2 intersect at (1,6), (2,3), (3,2). The parabola is higher on (1,2); the reciprocal curve is higher on (2,3).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the total area enclosed by the two curves.

answer.worked:
On $[1,2]$, the parabola is above the hyperbola. On $[2,3]$, the hyperbola is above the parabola.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\int_1^2\left(x^2-6x+11-\frac6x\right)\,dx+\int_2^3\left(\frac6x-x^2+6x-11\right)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-3x^2+11x-6\ln x\right]_1^2+\left[6\ln x-\frac{x^3}{3}+3x^2-11x\right]_2^3\\&=\left(\frac{13}{3}-6\ln2\right)+\left(6\ln\frac32-\frac73\right)\\&=2-6\ln\frac43\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
